original_abstract.text: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, offering a way to scale computation without increasing parameter count. However, full-stack looping places context construction and iterative state refinement within the same recurrent computation, without explicitly distinguishing their roles. We introduce the Asymmetric Looped Transformer (AsymLoop), which separates single-pass context encoding from recurrent state refinement. A single-pass causal encoder produces layer-specific Global key-value (KV) caches that remain fixed across iterations, while a weight-tied recurrent decoder generates Local KV from its evolving state. Joint attention over both sources under a single softmax allows each update to integrate persistent contextual information with the current intermediate state. For training, we apply a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate method to the encoder and decoder. Experiments on FineWeb-Edu across four model scales, from 60M to 1B, show consistently lower validation perplexity and higher average downstream accuracy than Full Loop under matched effective depth and training token budgets. At 1B, AsymLoop improves average zero-shot accuracy across seven commonsense reasoning benchmarks from 49.58% to 50.85%. Further experiments extend these benefits to longer training budgets, an OLMo-style backbone, and sparse mixture-of-experts models. These results support asymmetric context encoding and state refinement as an effective design for recurrent language models.
original_abstract.source_title: Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder

en.text: AsymLoop separates one-pass context encoding from recurrent state refinement. A causal encoder supplies fixed global KV caches, while a weight-tied decoder attends jointly to them and evolving local states. At matched effective depth and training tokens, models from 60M to 1B improve over full-stack looping. At 1B, average accuracy on seven commonsense benchmarks rises from 49.58% to 50.85%; recommendation transfer is untested.

zh.text: AsymLoop 将一次性上下文编码与循环状态更新分开：因果编码器提供固定的全局 KV 缓存，共享权重的解码器联合关注全局缓存和不断变化的局部状态。在有效深度和训练 token 数一致时，6000 万至 10 亿参数模型优于整栈循环；10 亿参数模型的七项常识基准平均准确率从 49.58% 升至 50.85%。推荐任务迁移尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval (GR) casts search and recommendation as autoregressive generation of discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs). SID design largely determines GR quality, but its discrete, interdependent components (SID construction, collision handling, decoding, and training) cannot be optimized end-to-end with gradients and remain largely hand-designed. We introduce a framework that improves these components through LLM-driven evolutionary program search, to our knowledge the first application of this approach to GR. A locally served, open-weight 31B model mutates executable GR components, so no proprietary LLM API is used, and a 1M-parameter proxy decoder provides fast feedback in place of repeatedly training the 1B target generator. Across 21 SID programs on NQ320K, proxy and target Recall@100 show strong rank correlation (Spearman $ρ= 0.90$). Guided by this proxy, evolution improves the seed GR on NQ320K, MSMARCO300K, and a multilingual e-commerce dataset under a fixed training recipe. On NQ320K, jointly evolving SID construction and collision handling improves Recall@1 from 55.8% to 59.3% and Recall@100 from 85.8% to 90.6%. A component study shows that proxy reliability depends on what is evolved: improvements transfer reliably for the semantic index but not for the generator's training objective or the full pipeline. LLM-driven evolutionary search is thus a practical tool for GR design, provided proxy reliability is established for the chosen search space.
original_abstract.source_title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval

en.text: This framework uses a locally served 31B language model to evolve semantic-index programs and a 1M proxy decoder to evaluate designs before training a 1B generator. On NQ320K, jointly evolving ID construction and collision handling raises Recall@1 from 55.8% to 59.3% and Recall@100 from 85.8% to 90.6%. Proxy gains transfer reliably for semantic indexes, but not for training objectives or the full pipeline.

zh.text: 该框架用本地部署的 310 亿参数语言模型演化语义索引程序，并用 100 万参数代理解码器评估方案，减少反复训练 10 亿参数生成器的需求。在 NQ320K 上，联合优化 ID 构建与碰撞处理，使 Recall@1 从 55.8% 升至 59.3%，Recall@100 从 85.8% 升至 90.6%。代理收益能可靠迁移到语义索引，但未能可靠迁移到训练目标或完整流水线。

original_abstract.text: Modeling lifetime user behavior sequences is essential for capturing long-range preferences in industrial recommendation, yet sequences containing up to 100K interactions make target-aware ranking prohibitively expensive. Search-based methods that retrieve from raw sequences incur candidate-dependent costs that grow with sequence length, whereas latent compression methods reduce computation at the expense of item-level addressability. We propose ECHO (Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators), a framework that balances efficiency and fine-grained retrieval by retaining a subset of original event records per user through a Distilled Selector (DS) and retrieving a smaller set of target-relevant records for each candidate through a Target-aware Fine-grained Retriever (TFR). DS is supervised by a candidate-aware full-history teacher via per-target distillation, enabling target-aware user-level selection without requiring full-history computation for every candidate. The retriever and target-attention scorer share the relevance parameters learned by the teacher, ensuring consistent relevance estimation throughout the cascade. At a sequence length of 100K, ECHO reduces online sequence-branch FLOPs by approximately 160 times compared with a representative end-to-end model. Three deployment optimizations, including common user inputs, compact record encoding, and key-side projection absorption, further reduce memory, storage, and data-movement overhead. Experiments on KuaiRand-1K and an industrial-scale short-video platform demonstrate relative GAUC improvements ranging from 0.113% to 1.520% over state-of-the-art baselines across multiple tasks. Furthermore, online A/B tests in two production scenarios, Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite, show that ECHO improves app usage time by 0.240% and 0.373%, respectively.
original_abstract.source_title: ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling

en.text: ECHO makes target-aware ranking over 100K user events practical by distilling a teacher into a user-level selector that retains raw records and a candidate-aware retriever with shared operator design. It reports roughly 160 times fewer online sequence-branch FLOPs than a representative end-to-end approach, with relative GAUC gains of 0.113–1.520% on KuaiRand and industrial data. Online Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite tests report usage-time gains of 0.240% and 0.373%.

zh.text: ECHO 为降低十万条用户行为上的目标感知排序成本，将教师知识蒸馏到保留原始记录的用户级选择器和候选感知检索器，两阶段采用同构算子。相对一个代表性的端到端方案，在线序列分支 FLOPs 约减少至 1/160；KuaiRand 与工业数据上的 GAUC 相对提升 0.113%–1.520%。快手与快手极速版在线测试的使用时长分别提升 0.240% 和 0.373%。

original_abstract.text: Multimodal click-through rate (CTR) prediction is central to search systems, where ranking depends on item content, query relevance, and user preference. Existing approaches incorporate content through dense embeddings or coarse discrete IDs, yet effectively integrating fine-grained heterogeneous content with ID-based predictors remains challenging. We propose FineSID, a progressive learning framework that unifies content tokenization, query--item semantic pretraining, and personalized post-training via a shared fine-grained discrete representation. Each stage optimizes an explicit objective while preserving token-level access to content. First, a pretrained multi-scale visual tokenizer and text tokenizers convert heterogeneous content into fine-grained Semantic IDs (SIDs), explicitly aligning them with the ID features. Second, full-parameter semantic pretraining under query--item relevance supervision establishes a robust matching prior, jointly optimizing the interactions of multimodal SIDs and conventional fields within a shared predictor. Third, this initialized predictor is directly fine-tuned with user click supervision to capture implicit personalized preferences. Extensive offline and online evaluations demonstrate substantial gains in both standard CTR prediction and core business metrics. Furthermore, FineSID improves within-product creative discrimination, demonstrating its semantic generalization beyond conventional ID memorization.
original_abstract.source_title: Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction

en.text: This progressive CTR framework connects content understanding, query relevance and personalization. Fine-grained visual and textual semantic IDs share a feature-interaction predictor with ID features; full-parameter query-item semantic pretraining precedes personalized click fine-tuning. Offline and online evaluations report improvements in CTR and business metrics, alongside within-product creative discrimination. The abstract supplies no numerical effect sizes.

zh.text: 该渐进式 CTR 框架衔接内容理解、查询相关性和个性化：细粒度视觉与文本语义 ID 和 ID 特征共用交互预测器，先进行全参数查询—商品语义预训练，再以个性化点击任务微调。离线和在线评测报告 CTR 与业务指标改善，并提升同商品创意区分能力。摘要未提供数值增益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommenders replace the retrieve-then-rank cascade with a single model: beam search over semantic item identifiers performs retrieval, and the same likelihood performs ranking. We show that this shared score makes them forget long-tail items twice. In retrieval, beam search keeps identifier prefixes by the probability mass of their subtrees, so tail items are pruned early, and a wider beam admits few more of them. In ranking, the likelihood places tail items below head items even when they are admitted, so expanding retrieval alone brings little or no gain. Both failures reflect missing item-level memorization (i.e., direct recall of which items co-occur), which collaborative filtering provides and shared-prefix generation lacks. To this end, we propose CAPE (Co-occurrence-Aware Pool Expansion), a training-free plug-in that restores memorization at both stages: (i) a memorization channel retrieves co-occurrence-supported tail items outside the beam and scores them with the frozen generator, and (ii) memorization-calibrated ranking fuses the generator likelihood with co-occurrence evidence while keeping the generator's first item. Experiments with two generative backbones on product and music domains show that CAPE significantly improves long-tail accuracy over the backbones and over re-ranking baselines that share its candidates, preserves or improves overall accuracy, and adds a small fraction of the latency.
original_abstract.source_title: Generative Recommenders Forget the Long Tail: Restoring Memorization in Retrieval and Ranking

en.text: CAPE addresses long-tail memorization lost by semantic-ID generative recommenders. A training-free co-occurrence candidate pool expands beyond beam-search results, and memorization-calibrated reranking preserves the generator’s top item. Experiments with two backbones on product and music recommendation improve tail retrieval and ranking. This complements generative generalization without retraining the generator; the abstract gives no numerical effect sizes.

zh.text: CAPE 针对语义 ID 生成式推荐丢失长尾记忆的问题，用无需训练的共现候选池补充束搜索结果，再以记忆校准重排保留生成器的首位商品。商品和音乐推荐上的两种骨干实验改善了长尾检索与排序。它无需重训生成器即可补充生成式泛化能力；摘要未给出数值增益。

original_abstract.text: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. These observations motivate a shift from fixed-depth computation to item-level adaptive reasoning. To this end, we propose LoopRec. LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block and introduces a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary that makes a binary exit-or-continue decision for every item independently. Items whose representations have sufficiently matured exit early, while those requiring deeper reasoning continue to subsequent recursions. This design converts the fixed global depth into a learned, per-item property without auxiliary depth labels, and is readily adaptable to diverse backbone architectures. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks with four backbone families demonstrate that LoopRec consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. Further analysis reveals that LoopRec's learned allocation exhibits interpretable patterns aligned with our post-hoc oracle analysis: lower-frequency items and more recent interactions naturally receive deeper computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec.
original_abstract.source_title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation

en.text: LoopRec allocates different amounts of recurrent computation to individual history items. A shared block and binary exit gate learn item-level depth without auxiliary depth labels. Across four sequential recommendation backbones on public benchmarks, adaptive recursion improves the quality-efficiency trade-off; analyses associate deeper computation with rare and recent items. The evidence does not establish industrial serving gains.

zh.text: LoopRec 为历史中的不同商品分配不同循环计算量，通过共享模块和二元退出门学习逐商品深度，无需额外深度标签。在公共基准的四种序列推荐骨干上，自适应循环改善了效果与效率的权衡；分析显示低频和近期商品往往获得更深计算。证据尚不能证明工业服务收益。

original_abstract.text: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, motivating their use as the backbone of foundation recommendation models (FRMs). Existing methods enhance recommendations through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning under a Think-then-Answer paradigm. However, explicit CoT incurs substantial inference overhead by generating lengthy reasoning traces and relies on manually designed templates that struggle to capture diverse, dynamic user interests. We propose OneLatent, an efficient latent reasoning framework that compresses explicit reasoning traces into several learnable latent tokens, enabling Latent-Reason-then-Answer inference without generating verbose traces. OneLatent first introduces Multi-View Adaptive CoT (MV-ACoT), which creates diverse, high-quality teacher-generated supervision by exploring user interests from multiple perspectives and automatically adapting reasoning complexity to each instance. Building on pretrained FRMs, it then uses a three-stage latent-token alignment paradigm to progressively internalize CoT traces into learnable latent tokens. Finally, a multistage curriculum-based post-training strategy activates latent-token reasoning for downstream recommendation tasks. Experiments on an industrial-scale Kuaishou dataset and the public Kuaishou LLM-Rec benchmark show that OneLatent consistently outperforms explicit CoT-based methods and traditional baselines. Compared with the Think and No-Think variants of FRMs, OneLatent improves SID@64 by 17.44% and 9.33%, respectively, while achieving over 17x higher online inference throughput. We further develop a production serving system for scalable, real-time FRM inference. An online A/B test in Kuaishou's local-services advertising scenario shows that deploying OneLatent with this system yields an estimated 9.6% revenue lift over strong online baselines, including OneRec and OneReason.
original_abstract.source_title: OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models

en.text: Compresses explicit recommendation Chain-of-Thought into a few learnable latent tokens to reduce reasoning-generation overhead. Multi-view adaptive teacher reasoning supplies supervision; three-stage latent-token alignment and curriculum-based post-training internalize and activate that reasoning. On industrial Kuaishou data and Kuaishou LLM-Rec, OneLatent reports SID@64 improvements of 17.44% and 9.33% over Think and No-Think FRM variants, respectively, alongside over 17× higher online inference throughput. An online local-services advertising test of OneLatent plus its production serving system estimates a 9.6% revenue lift over strong baselines including OneRec and OneReason. CTR scaling takeaway: latent reasoning offers a route to spend model capacity without long generated traces; SID and combined-system revenue results do not establish a CTR gain or isolate model-only online impact.

zh.text: 将推荐任务的显式思维链压缩为少量可学习隐式 token，以降低生成推理文本的开销。方法先通过多视角自适应教师推理生成监督，再用三阶段隐式 token 对齐和课程式后训练内化并激活推理能力。在快手工业数据和 Kuaishou LLM-Rec 上，OneLatent 相比 FRM 的 Think、No-Think 变体，SID@64 分别提升 17.44% 和 9.33%，并报告在线推理吞吐量提高超过 17 倍。快手本地生活广告在线测试中，OneLatent 与配套生产服务系统联合部署，相对包含 OneRec、OneReason 的强基线取得估计 9.6% 的收入提升。对 CTR scaling 的启发：隐式推理有望在不生成长推理文本的情况下利用模型能力；SID 指标和联合系统收入收益不能直接证明 CTR 提升，也不能单独归因于模型。

original_abstract.text: General-purpose embeddings trained on profile similarity often misrank candidates in professional networks, where relevance is inherently complementary rather than symmetric. For example, job seekers usually engage with recruiters rather than peers with similar credentials. Current user recommendation systems are often built on profile similarity or social signals such as shared connections, which are effective in friend-oriented social networks where users tend to connect with similar people or within existing social circles. However, this does not hold in professional platforms like LinkedIn, where interactions are often goal-driven and cross-role interactions, requiring matching based on complementary intents rather than similarity or social proximity. In this paper, we propose Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval, a retrieval framework that is designed to model user intent preference instead of profile similarity. Our approach is inspired by the preference-learning perspective of Direct Preference Optimization, but instantiates preference learning as an exposure-conditioned multi-negative contrastive objective over embeddings. This formulation simplifies training and scales efficiently to large candidate sets without requiring an explicit reference model. Furthermore, we incorporate user interaction history by aggregating click histories with positional encoding to capture temporal order, which enables constant-cost updates of user representations over a fixed history window, allowing new interactions to be incorporated without re-encoding history. As a result, personalization can be updated efficiently using lightweight CPU operations without repeated LLM inference during serving. We evaluate PAIR on LinkedIn's Premium retrieval task. A 0.6B parameter model achieves a MAR@100 of 0.45.
original_abstract.source_title: PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn

en.text: PAIR models complementary professional intent rather than profile similarity for people retrieval. An exposure-conditioned multi-negative contrastive objective learns preferences, while position-aware click-history aggregation permits constant-cost updates within a fixed history window. A 0.6B-parameter model reaches MAR@100 of 0.45 on LinkedIn Premium retrieval. Lightweight CPU updates avoid repeated language-model inference during personalization; the abstract reports no online business lift.

zh.text: PAIR 在人员检索中建模互补职业意图，而非仅匹配档案相似度。曝光条件下的多负例对比目标学习偏好，带位置编码的点击历史聚合支持固定历史窗口内的常数成本更新。6 亿参数模型在 LinkedIn Premium 检索任务上达到 MAR@100 0.45；轻量 CPU 更新避免个性化时反复调用语言模型，摘要未报告在线业务增益。

original_abstract.text: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models. On block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin. For visual token merging, it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.
original_abstract.source_title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

en.text: TTR-Compressor treats sequence compression as learned test-time regression, computing closed-form coefficients during the forward pass. It supports blockwise attention and visual-token merging. Experiments report strong RULER results, while a visual merger matches an MLP merger with 55.6% fewer tokens. These results concern long-context and multimodal models, with no recommendation-specific evaluation.

zh.text: TTR-Compressor 将序列压缩表述为可学习的测试时回归，在前向过程中求闭式系数，支持分块注意力与视觉 token 合并。实验报告了较强的 RULER 表现；视觉合并器用少 55.6% 的 token 匹配 MLP 合并器效果。结果来自长上下文和多模态模型，没有推荐专门评测。

original_abstract.text: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously observed "slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.
original_abstract.source_title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy

en.text: This work identifies floating-point errors in softmax and cross-entropy: target gradients can round to zero, and near-matching teacher and student distributions can suffer cancellation. Revised implementations suppress the Slingshot effect and distillation drift in the reported experiments. The contribution improves numerical behavior of common training operators; recommendation-specific gains are not established.

zh.text: 该研究指出 softmax 和交叉熵中的浮点误差：目标梯度可能被舍入为零，接近的教师与学生分布也可能出现相消误差。修正实现抑制了所报告实验中的 Slingshot 现象和蒸馏漂移。其意义在于改善常用训练算子的数值行为，尚未证明推荐任务上的收益。

original_abstract.text: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Learned sparse attention is a promising architecture for million-token contexts, widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2. Selection, however, grows into the training bottleneck. For each query, it scores every previous token whereas sparse attention reads only $k$; worse, current systems materialize a full score table and repeat selection during recomputation. Our key insight is that the output of selection is not an activation, but rather a set of indices. Building on it, HyScale introduces FlashTopK and selection replay. FlashTopK finds each query's exact top-$k$ on the fly without a score table, while selection replay reuses forward-pass selection in recomputation. Together with holistic system optimizations tackling end-to-end challenges, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by $2.07\times$ over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs. It also speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by $2.01\times$ and $1.57\times$ at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.
original_abstract.source_title: HyScale: Scaling Long-Context Training for Learned Sparse Attention

en.text: HyScale targets the selection bottleneck in learned sparse-attention training. FlashTopK computes exact top-k indices without materializing the score table, and selection replay reuses forward selections during recomputation. With other system optimizations, it speeds up million-token GLM-5.1 training by 2.07 times over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs; additional results measure individual attention layers on 32 H800 GPUs. The selection and recomputation design is relevant to long-sequence training engineering, with no CTR benchmark claimed.

zh.text: HyScale处理可学习稀疏注意力训练中的选择瓶颈：FlashTopK不保存完整分数表，直接求精确top-k索引；选择重放则在重计算阶段复用前向选择结果。结合其他系统优化，在512张H20上，百万token序列的GLM-5.1训练速度为Megatron-LM的2.07倍；另有在32张H800上测量单独注意力层的结果。其选择与重计算设计可供长序列训练工程参考，论文未验证CTR收益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommenders using semantic identifiers predict items through successive token decisions, but beam search may irreversibly prune promising item paths. This limitation is particularly consequential when a few recent interactions signal an emerging interest while earlier behavior favors established preferences. Yet an independently trained discriminative recommender may rank the same items highly from the same interaction history. Such complementary scores are available at test time, offering a way to adapt a frozen generator without retraining either model. The challenge is to use these scores before pruning: combining completed recommendation lists cannot alter earlier beam decisions, while scores over complete items cannot directly inform choices among semantic prefixes shared by multiple items. We propose \textbf{T}est-Time \textbf{C}ollaborative \textbf{B}eam \textbf{S}earch \textbf{A}daptation (\textbf{TCBSA}), a training-free method that incorporates collaborative information into semantic decoding. TCBSA transforms discriminative score margins into potentials over shared semantic edges and uses a confidence gate to regulate their contributions to cumulative path scores before beam selection. We establish a sufficient condition for target prefix survival under global beam competition and bound score perturbations under low discriminative confidence. Full-catalog experiments show consistent improvements over strong baselines across datasets and different generative and discriminative recommenders. Analyses of emerging interests and decoding behavior demonstrate gains in recommendation accuracy and target path survival, while targeted interventions support the contribution of shared prefix corrections. TCBSA also offers a favorable balance between recommendation accuracy and inference latency compared with simply widening the native beam.
original_abstract.source_title: From Item Scores to Semantic Tokens: Test-Time Collaborative Adaptation for Generative Recommendation

en.text: TCBSA adapts generative retrieval at test time using a frozen discriminative recommender. It projects item scores onto shared semantic-ID edges and applies confidence-gated potentials before beam pruning. Full-catalog experiments improve retrieval with a favorable latency trade-off compared with widening the beam. The method adds collaborative evidence without retraining the generator; the abstract gives no numerical effect sizes.

zh.text: TCBSA 在测试时用冻结的判别式推荐器适配生成式检索，将商品分数投影到共享语义 ID 边，并在束剪枝前加入置信度门控势值。全商品库实验改善了检索效果，相比扩大束宽具有较好的延迟权衡。它无需重训生成器即可引入协同证据；摘要未提供数值增益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation and predicts these codes to generate recommendations. Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item. Although such supervision identifies the target, it provides no explicit distributional information about alternative items conditioned on the same user history. Sequential recommenders can supply this item-level predictive knowledge, but transferring it to semantic-ID generation is challenging because the teacher and student operate in item and code spaces, respectively. We propose two complementary knowledge-distillation objectives for parallel semantic-ID recommenders, which predict all code positions simultaneously without autoregressive prefix conditioning. Item Distribution Matching (IDM) reconstructs a catalogue-level item distribution from the student's parallel code predictions and aligns it with the teacher's item distribution. Code Marginal Matching (CMM) projects the teacher's item probabilities onto each code position using fixed item-to-code assignments, then matches the resulting code marginals to the corresponding student heads. Both objectives transfer the teacher's soft distributional knowledge while preserving the student's parallel prediction structure. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that both methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches. On average, IDM improves Recall@10 by 15.39%, while CMM improves NDCG@10 by 8.28%. These results demonstrate that distillation in either reconstructed item space or code-marginal space can substantially strengthen hard-label supervision for parallel generative recommendation.
original_abstract.source_title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation

en.text: This work distills an item-space teacher into parallel semantic-ID generation, which avoids conditioning on previously generated codes. Item Distribution Matching reconstructs item probabilities, while Code Marginal Matching projects teacher distributions onto code marginals. Reported mean gains are 15.39% in Recall@10 for the former and 8.28% in NDCG@10 for the latter. The methods connect item-level knowledge with parallel code prediction.

zh.text: 该研究将商品空间教师蒸馏到并行语义 ID 生成器，避免依赖已经生成的码。Item Distribution Matching 重建商品概率，Code Marginal Matching 将教师分布投影到码的边缘分布。前者报告 Recall@10 平均提升 15.39%，后者报告 NDCG@10 平均提升 8.28%，为商品级知识与并行码预测建立联系。

original_abstract.text:
Generative recommenders retrieve items by writing their semantic IDs (SIDs) code by code under trie-constrained beam search, an approach now deployed on large web platforms. Standard autoregressive interfaces pay for the SID length K twice: a history of T items enters the backbone as TK code tokens, and every beam-search step runs through the backbone, so returning B candidates costs O(BK) backbone decode tokens per user. The second cost often dominates, and it grows with the backbone, the SID depth and the candidate budget.
  We introduce Deco (decoding from concepts), which separates reading the history from writing the identifier. The backbone reads each history item as one fused token and condenses the history once into a compact next-item concept; a light KV-cached decoder conditioned on the concept and the generated prefix runs the entire beam search, while the identifiers, the trie and the autoregressive factorization stay unchanged. The decoder approaches full-backbone accuracy with cross-entropy alone, and distillation improves it further. On seven datasets from e-commerce, movies and music streaming, Deco achieves comparable or better accuracy than both a standard generative recommender and the full-backbone teacher with fused inputs, while delivering 3.2-8.6$\times$ their throughput under a 50 ms p95 latency budget in a production-style serving pipeline. Delegating beam search makes larger candidate pools and models practical: Deco generates 1000 candidates faster than its teacher generates 100, and with a 1.5B-parameter LLM backbone, it matches the 69M-parameter teacher's throughput while achieving higher accuracy.
original_abstract.source_title: Separating Thinking from Spelling for Efficient Generative Recommendation

en.text: Deco separates history reasoning from semantic-ID decoding: each history item becomes one fused token, a heavy backbone produces one next-item concept, and a lightweight cached decoder performs beam search. On seven recommendation datasets it matches or improves the compared models while delivering 3.2–8.6 times their throughput under a 50 ms p95 budget in a production-style pipeline. The result supports larger candidate pools and backbones through cheaper decoding; it is not an online business-lift claim.

zh.text: Deco 将历史建模与语义标识符解码分开：每个历史物品合并为一个令牌，重骨干一次生成下一物品的概念表示，再由带缓存的轻量解码器执行束搜索。在七个推荐数据集上，其效果达到或超过所比较模型，并在生产式流水线的 p95 50 毫秒预算下获得 3.2–8.6 倍吞吐。该结果说明降低解码成本可支持更大的候选池和骨干，不代表已验证的线上业务收益。

original_abstract.text: As LLMs scale, mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures increase model capacity while keeping per-token computation manageable through sparse expert activation. This sparsity also enables memory-efficient deployment by retaining most expert weights in CPU memory and transferring or executing only the routed experts on demand. Existing MoE offloading systems typically target specific model-platform configurations, yet differences in model sparsity, CPU and GPU throughput, VRAM capacity, and host-device bandwidth can change the policy ranking. Because implementing and exhaustively evaluating all candidate policies incurs substantial engineering cost, efficiently selecting the best-performing policy for each model-platform configuration remains a key challenge for practical MoE offloading. We present COPE (Composable Offloading Policy Emulator), which selects the best-performing MoE offloading policy for a target model-platform configuration before runtime integration. COPE comprises two components. Its Policy Matrix factors the design space into two independent axes, expert residency and MoE execution strategy, enabling mechanism reuse across candidate policies and exposing four new candidates. Its Virtual Heterogeneous Machine profiles combined-operator schedules on the target platform and combines these measurements with offline routing traces to estimate candidate performance. Compared with the evaluated baselines, COPE improves fastest-policy selection accuracy by 24%-100% and reduces performance-prediction error by $1.7\times$ to $6.8\times$. By identifying the preferred policy before integration, COPE further reduces policy-specific implementation effort by up to 74%.
original_abstract.source_title: COPE: Composable Performance Emulation for Mixture-of-Experts Offloading Policies

en.text: COPE selects a MoE offloading policy for a target model and hardware platform before implementing it in the runtime. It separates expert residency from execution strategy, then combines profiles of operator schedules with offline routing traces to predict candidate performance. Against evaluated baselines, it reports better fastest-policy selection and lower prediction error, with policy-specific implementation effort reduced by up to 74%. The transferable idea is to choose offloading around actual memory, compute and bandwidth limits; the reported gains concern policy selection and integration effort, not model accuracy or CTR throughput.

zh.text: COPE 在接入运行系统之前，为目标模型与硬件平台选择 MoE 卸载策略。它把专家驻留位置和执行方式分开组合，再结合算子调度的实测性能与离线路由轨迹，估计各候选方案的表现。相对所比较的基线，论文报告最佳策略选择更准、性能预测误差更低，特定策略的实现工作量最高减少 74%。可借鉴的是按实际内存、算力和带宽约束选方案；这些收益指策略选择与集成成本，不是模型准确率或 CTR 吞吐提升。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval replaces nearest-neighbor search with token-by-token decoding of an item's semantic ID (SID). But existing SID-based methods primarily use L levels of tokens sequentially to represent each item in the input history. As a result, a fixed context window holds L times fewer items than it would with one embedding per item. We present PinGER, a generative retriever deployed at Pinterest that retains SID outputs while making input histories compact, built on three ideas. (1) An asymmetric attention mask over interleaved SID and dense tokens lets later items attend only to the dense ones, so the model is supervised at every SID position in training yet serves one token per item while computing the same function. (2) Generation is controllable through goal-conditioned outputs, reinforcement learning, and a prefix-diversity penalty, which together steer retrieval toward surface-specific goals and diverse candidates. (3) A serving stack built for efficient wide-beam generation is paired with decoding constrained to valid identifiers and candidate resolution from a host-local index. Deployed in Related Pins, PinGER lifts saves of fresh Pins by 3.60% and overall saves by 0.62%, while reducing the surface's end-to-end latency by 0.7% and eliminating the cost of the nearest-neighbor search it replaces.
original_abstract.source_title: PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs

en.text: PinGER retains semantic-ID outputs while serving one token per history item. An asymmetric mask preserves the training function, goal-conditioned generation and diversity controls steer retrieval, and wide-beam serving resolves valid IDs through a local index. Deployment in Pinterest Related Pins increases fresh-Pin saves by 3.60% and overall saves by 0.62%, reduces end-to-end surface latency by 0.7%, and removes the replaced nearest-neighbor search cost.

zh.text: PinGER 保留语义 ID 输出，同时在服务时将每条历史商品压缩为一个 token。非对称掩码保持训练函数一致，目标条件生成和多样性控制引导检索，宽束服务通过本地索引解析有效 ID。在 Pinterest Related Pins 部署中，新鲜 Pin 保存量提升 3.60%、整体保存量提升 0.62%，页面端到端延迟降低 0.7%，并消除了被替代近邻搜索的成本。

original_abstract.text: The key-value (KV) cache places growing demands on GPU memory capacity and bandwidth as large language models serve longer contexts and more concurrent requests. Its footprint limits concurrency, while repeated KV reads during attention can make decoding memory-bandwidth bound. Prior lossless KV cache compression methods reduce transfers between devices but restore the uncompressed KV cache in GPU memory before attention. They therefore leave these repeated KV reads unchanged and require additional work and memory for decompression. We present ZipFusion, which enables attention to consume the losslessly compressed KV cache directly. ZipFusion co-designs the compression format and attention kernel to reduce the bytes read from GPU memory during attention. The kernel reconstructs the original values directly in registers using simple bit operations, avoiding a separate decompression pass and easing the memory-bandwidth bound. ZipFusion also reassigns memory freed by compression across layers to store additional KV cache. Its memory manager reserves space for ongoing generation and makes the remaining capacity available to new requests. We implement ZipFusion on top of FlashInfer and integrate it with SGLang. On an NVIDIA H100, ZipFusion achieves about 1.25x speedup over FlashInfer in decode attention. With 8K context, it improves model decode throughput by up to 26.3% over uncompressed SGLang under the same GPU memory budget. At each method's largest supported batch, it also delivers up to 2.76x the throughput of the best-performing lossless KV cache compression baseline.
original_abstract.source_title: ZipFusion: Fusing Lossless KV Decompression with Attention for Efficient LLM Decoding

en.text: ZipFusion co-designs a lossless KV format and attention kernel so compressed values are reconstructed directly in registers, avoiding a separate decompression pass and reducing GPU memory reads. Integrated with FlashInfer and SGLang, it reports about 1.25x decode-attention speed on H100 and up to 26.3% higher model decoding throughput at 8K context under the same GPU-memory budget. The up-to-2.76x comparison uses each lossless-compression baseline at its largest supported batch.

zh.text: ZipFusion联合设计无损KV格式与注意力内核，在寄存器中直接恢复原值，省去单独解压过程并减少显存读取。它基于FlashInfer并接入SGLang，在H100上报告约1.25倍的解码注意力速度；同等显存预算、8K上下文下，模型解码吞吐最多提升26.3%。相对其他无损压缩方案最高2.76倍的结果采用各自可支持的最大batch。

original_abstract.text: Transformers achieve strong performance across modalities but are bottlenecked by the quadratic cost of attention. Sparse attention can reduce this cost, but effective sparsity must preserve useful long-range communication and map well to GPU hardware. We introduce INTRA--Interleaved Non-contiguous Token spaRse Attention--a hardware-aware static sparse attention design based on a relay-communication view under Computational Query Set (CQS) constraints. Rather than directly covering all token-to-token interactions within each sparse layer, INTRA uses complementary sparse groups to provide short mediated communication paths across layers. Scatter forms relay groups that sample broadly across local neighborhoods, while Gather reconnects these groups in subsequent layers. Under a partition model, this structure guides CQS-compatible sparse patterns with global reachability. Our CQS-aware FlashAttention-style kernel computes structured indices at runtime, loads selected non-contiguous tokens, and packs them densely for computation. On an A100, INTRA achieves a $1.53\times$ speedup in $2K$ FLUX.1-dev generation, with better measured image quality than evaluated CLEAR configurations after LoRA self-distillation. On LLaMA-3.1-8B, it improves long-context prefill efficiency with strong teacher-forced retrieval performance under matched LoRA adaptation. Attention-only benchmarks further show up to $8.4\times$ and $10.4\times$ speedups over MoBA and density-constrained NSA, respectively.
original_abstract.source_title: INTRA: Interleaved Non-contiguous Token spaRse Attention

en.text: INTRA uses complementary Scatter and Gather sparse token groups to relay information across layers, with a GPU kernel that packs non-contiguous tokens for computation. After adaptation, it reports a 1.53-fold FLUX.1-dev generation speedup on an A100 and improved long-context prefill efficiency for LLaMA-3.1-8B. Larger reported gains are attention-only benchmarks, not end-to-end speedups. Its hardware-aware static pattern offers a transferable sparse-attention design; CTR performance is unverified.

zh.text: INTRA 以互补的 Scatter 和 Gather 稀疏令牌组跨层传递信息，并由 GPU 内核将不连续令牌打包计算。经过适配后，它在 A100 上报告 FLUX.1-dev 生成加速 1.53 倍，并改善 LLaMA-3.1-8B 的长上下文预填充效率。论文中更大的加速数字来自纯注意力基准，不能视为端到端收益。其硬件感知静态模式可供稀疏注意力设计参考，CTR 效果尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Large language models (LLMs) bring world knowledge to user preference modeling in sequential recommendation, but generation-based recommenders express next-item predictions indirectly as text. Generated outputs may fail to identify a unique candidate item, depend on candidate presentation order in the prompt, and lack explicit confidence in the recommendation. Recent studies explore Jev, a model for fast option selection with explicit confidence. Inspired by Jev, we introduce decision-native recommendation, a new paradigm that jointly models item choice and recommendation confidence using LLM representations. It requires valid candidate selection, consistency under candidate reordering, and confidence that reflects recommendation accuracy. We propose Direct Item Choice Estimation (DICE), which learns a personalized next-item distribution over supplied candidates from user interaction history and recommends the highest-scoring item with calibrated confidence. Tree-structured attention shares history computation across isolated candidate branches for order-consistent candidate scoring in a single forward pass. On three recommendation datasets, DICE achieves higher top-one accuracy than all evaluated baselines. Separate evaluations show unchanged item choices under tested candidate reorderings and end-to-end speedups of up to approximately $6\times$ over the evaluated generation-based methods. Its confidence estimates support selective recommendation by identifying more reliable predictions and guide additional computation for low-confidence examples in offline routing.
original_abstract.source_title: Decision-Native Recommendation with Large Language Models

en.text: DICE directly estimates a next-item distribution and confidence over supplied candidates instead of expressing the choice as generated text. Tree-structured attention shares history computation while isolating candidate branches, enabling order-consistent scoring in one forward pass. On three recommendation datasets, it reports the highest top-one accuracy among evaluated baselines, unchanged choices under tested reorderings, and up to roughly sixfold end-to-end speedup over evaluated generation-based methods. Confidence supports selective recommendation and offline allocation of extra compute, offering a candidate-scoring design rather than a demonstrated full-catalog or online result.

zh.text: DICE 直接对给定候选估计下一物品分布与置信度，省去用生成文本表达选择的过程。树状注意力让候选分支共享历史计算、彼此隔离，在一次前向中完成对候选顺序稳定的打分。三个推荐数据集上，作者报告所比较方法中最高的首位准确率，测试中的候选重排不改变选择，相对生成式方法端到端速度最高约为 6 倍。置信度还用于选择性推荐和离线分配额外计算；这些结果不等于全目录或线上验证。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation formulates item recommendation as autoregressive generation rather than a discriminative scoring problem. Although empirical studies exhibit favorable scaling behavior in recommendation, unleashing the benefits of scaling remains challenging under the strict model size and inference cost constraints of real-world systems. A central challenge is to combine expressive modeling of user-item interaction histories with flexible computational depth without proportionally increasing model size. We introduce LoopGR, a parameter-efficient scaling framework for generative recommendation via recurrent depth. LoopGR employs a tailored hierarchical recurrent depth mechanism that alternates between a shared generative decoder and a lightweight context updater. For efficient inference, we further develop recurrent trajectory self-distillation that distills a low-budget student from a high-budget teacher by aligning both predictive distributions and evolution directions. Extensive experiments show that LoopGR consistently outperforms strong generative recommendation baselines. Compared with a representative encoder-decoder baseline, LoopGR achieves superior performance while reducing model size by up to 52%. These results establish recurrent depth as a new scaling dimension, offering a flexible and resource-efficient scaling path for generative recommendation.
original_abstract.source_title: LoopGR: Parameter-Efficient Scaling for Generative Recommendation via Recurrent Depth

en.text: LoopGR increases generative recommendation depth without proportionally increasing parameters. A shared generative decoder alternates with a lightweight context updater, while recurrent trajectory self-distillation aligns predictions and evolution directions between high- and low-budget runs. Experiments outperform strong baselines and reduce model size by up to 52% relative to a representative encoder-decoder. The result concerns parameter-efficient scaling, not a quantified production latency gain.

zh.text: LoopGR 在不同比增加参数的情况下加深生成式推荐计算：共享生成解码器与轻量上下文更新器交替执行，再用循环轨迹自蒸馏对齐高、低预算运行的预测与演化方向。实验优于强基线，相对一个代表性的编码器—解码器，模型大小最多减少 52%。结果支持参数高效扩展，并未量化生产延迟收益。

original_abstract.text: Session-based recommendation (SBR) infers user interest from limited interaction sequences, yet current models show a consistent performance drop when longer histories are available. This degradation is associated with decoder designs that overemphasize recent items while underutilizing distant, yet semantically relevant, interactions, leading to poor modeling of long-range dependencies and multi-interest behaviors. To address this challenge, we introduce MIDA (Multi-Interest Decoding with Adaptive Aggregation for Session-based Recommendation), a lightweight and encoder-agnostic framework that provides a reformulation of the decoding stage. The central design principle is a two-space decoupling: clustering operates on raw item embeddings so that semantic groupings are not distorted by encoder-learned relational biases; encoder outputs are reserved for aggregation, where sequential context remains intact. Concretely, MIDA (i) employs differentiable multi-interest clustering on raw embeddings, preserving semantic structure that encoder representations would otherwise obscure, and (ii) fuses stability and plasticity branches through a gate conditioned on average cluster size, so that the inferred clustering structure directly governs aggregation behavior through a structural coupling across the two stages. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MIDA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with meaningful accuracy improvements while remaining computationally practical.
original_abstract.source_title: MIDA: Multi-Interest Decoding with Adaptive Aggregation for Session-based Recommendation

en.text: Uses raw-embedding interest clustering and cluster-size-conditioned aggregation to improve session recommendation with longer histories. The encoder-agnostic decoder separates semantic grouping from contextual aggregation; reported gains are on benchmark datasets, not industrial online traffic.

zh.text: 针对较长会话中远期兴趣被忽略的问题，MIDA在原始物品嵌入上聚类，再按簇规模门控聚合编码器输出。语义分组与序列上下文分工处理，多个离线基准显示收益，可作为长历史兴趣聚合模块参考。

original_abstract.text: Speculative decoding checks several drafted tokens in one verification pass. On a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, consecutive tokens often select the same experts. A deduplicating engine reads each selected expert once per pass, so it requests fewer bytes than a per-slot engine, which reads it once per token. We write a step's time as the bytes each kernel requests over its effective bandwidth, plus fixed time. Under geometric acceptance, we derive from this step time when speculation is faster than plain decoding. The best draft length is a monotone staircase in the acceptance rate. We bound how a bandwidth error moves each result, and we check the main steps in Lean. Deduplication is faster exactly where its share $\bar u(n)$ of the per-slot bytes is below its ratio $r(n)$ of the per-slot bandwidth. On llama.cpp Metal, MLX-LM and llama.cpp CUDA, which we modified to deduplicate, the per-slot kernel has the higher effective bandwidth (r = 0.32 to 0.75). Thus deduplication is faster only from 5 to 8 tokens per pass, or never. We fit the bandwidths on one layer's expert operation, run alone, in under an hour per model. Bytes from routing traces over these bandwidths predict the time that deduplication saves. The measured saving lies inside its error bound at every point on CUDA and MLX-LM and at 36 of 48 points on Metal. The crossover is the first pass size at which deduplication is faster. The prediction places it within one pass size in 10 of 12 configurations of engine, model and depth. We computed these predictions after the measurements. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, operation times measured before its speculative runs give the best draft length on CUDA within one at all 22 acceptance values.
original_abstract.source_title: Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts Models: Expert Bytes, Kernel Bandwidth and the Best Draft Length

en.text: Models MoE speculative verification time using requested expert bytes, effective kernel bandwidth and fixed overhead. Measured engines show that deduplicating expert reads can lose bandwidth efficiency, so fewer bytes do not always mean lower latency; the model estimates crossover points and draft lengths with explicit error bounds.

zh.text: 把MoE推测验证时间拆为专家读取字节数、有效内核带宽和固定开销，推导去重读取的收益条件与草稿长度选择。多个执行引擎的实验说明去重也可能降低带宽效率，适用于专家复用优化前的延迟建模与实测校准。

original_abstract.text: Estimating neural scaling laws involves an end-to-end pipeline: designing a scaling recipe, training models across scales, evaluating models on a target metric, and deploying an algorithm to fit a scaling law to the resulting data. This final fitting stage is often treated as routine: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss using local optimization from a grid of initializations, and return the best solution found. Yet such heuristic searches can fail in two distinct ways: they offer no guarantee of returning a nearly optimal solution, and they obscure whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. Indeed, we show that standard scaling law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect (Breiman, 2001): the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. We resolve these issues with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and exhaustively maps the near-minimizers to the implied range of scaling curves.
original_abstract.source_title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation

en.text: Ambiguous Fits examines the final fitting stage of neural scaling laws, where different parameter settings can fit observed data nearly equally well yet diverge in large-scale extrapolation. It replaces heuristic local searches with deterministic branch-and-bound optimization that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and maps near-minimizers to a range of implied scaling curves. This provides a way to expose fitting ambiguity when planning ranking-model scale; the guarantee concerns fitting loss, not accurate extrapolation or demonstrated CTR performance.

zh.text: Ambiguous Fits 关注 scaling law 的最后拟合环节：不同参数可能同样贴合已有实验数据，却对更大规模给出明显不同的预测。论文用确定性的分支定界算法替代启发式局部搜索，保证拟合损失接近最优，并把近似最优参数集合映射为一组可能的扩展曲线。它为规划排序模型规模时识别拟合歧义提供方法；保证针对的是拟合损失，并不保证外推准确，也未验证 CTR 效果。

original_abstract.text: Generative bundle construction completes a partially observed bundle by generating its missing items from a large product catalog. Compared to autoregressive LLMs, diffusion LLM emerges as a natural fit for this unordered generation task. Their bidirectional attention provides an inductive bias better aligned with unordered bundle construction. Iterative denoising can reveal multiple tokens per step, potentially reducing inference latency. However, directly applying DLMs to this task presents two key challenges: 1 Despite its flexible reveal order, confidence-guided decoding tends to postpone semantic-fork decisions until refinement tokens constrain their choices, reducing bundle diversity. 2 Revealing more tokens per step can compromise recommendation quality, stifling the potential for faster inference. We introduce DPE-Rec, a diffusion framework for diversity preservation and efficient recommendation. DPE-Rec preserves diversity by introducing semantic-fork-aware GRPO, which prioritizes semantic-fork decisions via autoregressive rollouts. It improves efficiency through pseudo-trajectory distillation, which concentrates learning from the vast random corruption space onto the compact trajectory-induced subspace visited by high-quality decoding, unlocking reliable multi-token decoding. Together, these components enable diverse and accurate bundle construction with substantially fewer denoise steps. Experiments on multiple bundle construction benchmarks show that DPE-Rec improves recommendation performance by 63% on average, and its fast variant achieves 25.6$times$ faster inference on average than existing generative recommendation arts, with minimal loss in recommendation quality.
original_abstract.source_title: DPE-Rec: Diversity-Preserving and Efficient Diffusion Language Model Recommendation for Bundle Construction

en.text: DPE-Rec uses diffusion language models to complete partially observed item bundles. Semantic-fork-aware GRPO prioritizes decisions that determine different bundle compositions, while pseudo-trajectory distillation concentrates training on states reached by high-quality decoding so more tokens can be revealed per step. Experiments report improved bundle recommendation, and a fast variant averages 25.6 times faster inference than evaluated generative recommenders with little quality loss. The evidence concerns bundle construction, offering a way to trade denoising steps against recommendation diversity and quality rather than a validated CTR speedup.

zh.text: DPE-Rec 用扩散语言模型补全商品组合：针对会决定不同组合方向的关键选择设计 GRPO 训练，再用伪轨迹蒸馏聚焦高质量解码经过的状态，使每一步可以可靠地确定更多 token。组合推荐实验报告了效果改善，快速版本相对所比较的生成式推荐方法平均推理速度达到 25.6 倍，同时只损失少量质量。可借鉴的是协同调整去噪步数、多样性和推荐效果；这些证据来自组合构建任务，不能直接当作 CTR 加速。
